 A Tundra owner who bought his truck from Carvana on October 1 took it in for an alignment and learned it needed a new engine under recall. Here’s how to check if your Toyota Tundra is affected and why used trucks can still be sold with open recalls. 
 Advertising 
 October 19, 2026 - 2:46PM EDT 
 By: Armen Hareyan 
 A 2023 Toyota Tundra owner who took his truck in for a simple alignment learned 10 minutes later that the dealer was replacing his engine, because his VIN still had open recalls, including Toyota's engine replacement recall for 2022 and 2023 non hybrid Tundras. If you own one of these trucks or are shopping for a used one, check the VIN for open recalls today, because used vehicles can legally be sold with unrepaired recalls, which is why buying a used 2023 Tundra without its engine recall history is such a big risk.
 Josh Carrigan shared his surprise two days ago in the 2023-2027 Toyota Tundra Owners public group on Facebook. His truck has about 45,000 miles, and he had owned it for less than three weeks.
 What Happened at the Dealership? 
 "Brought the truck in to get an alignment after the leveling kit, and 10 minutes later they walked in and told me they're giving me a new motor. What a wild turn of events for today," Josh wrote.
 When another member asked whether the service staff talked with him before checking the engine, Josh explained what happened. "They did not. He walked in and said there were 4 recalls for my truck and that they were going swap the motor and gave me a rental for a few weeks. I just got the truck on the 1st of the month."
 Josh said his Tundra is a 2023 non hybrid, and that he bought it from Carvana, which delivered it on October 1. That timing is the most important part of his story for anyone buying a used truck.
 Why Did the Dealer Find the Recall So Fast? 
 Toyota dealers check a vehicle's VIN for open recalls when it comes in for service, even for routine work like an alignment. That is why open recalls often surface during an unrelated visit, and it is likely what happened here.
 It also means the recall was open when Josh took delivery. He did not need to do anything wrong for that to happen, because used vehicles are not required to have recalls completed before they are sold.
 What Is the Tundra Engine Replacement Recall? 
 In May 2024, Toyota recalled 102,092 vehicles, including 98,568 Tundra pickups and 3,524 Lexus LX600 SUVs from the 2022 and 2023 model years, because machining debris may have been left inside the engine during manufacturing. The remedy is a free engine replacement, and the recall is filed with NHTSA as campaign 24V381 .
 Only the non hybrid 3.5 liter twin turbo V6 is affected, and hybrid i-FORCE MAX trucks are not part of this recall. Josh's truck is a 2023 non hybrid, which fits the recall population.
 Advertising 
 Toyota later expanded its effort. A second recall in late 2025 covered about 127,000 more 2022 to 2024 Tundra, Lexus LX and 2024 Lexus GX vehicles , and for those trucks dealers first inspect the main bearing with software and replace the engine if it cannot be confirmed as sound, The Drive reported .
 Signs of the problem can include:
 Engine knocking or unusual noise
 Rough idle or running
 Stalling or loss of power
 In rare cases, sudden engine failure while driving
 The scale of the job is huge. Toyota has faced a monumental task replacing nearly 100,000 Tundra engines , and dealers have had to schedule the work as replacement engines become available.
 How Do I Check If My Tundra Has the Engine Recall? 
 It takes about a minute. Here is how:
 Find your 17 character VIN on the driver side dashboard, the door jamb sticker or your registration
 Enter it at nhtsa.gov/recalls to see every open safety recall
 Check Toyota's owner website or the Toyota app for Toyota specific campaigns
 Call your Toyota dealer's service department and ask them to run the VIN
 Ask for a printout showing open and completed recalls for your records
 If your truck shows an open engine recall, call your dealer right away to get in line. Even if parts are not ready, being on the list matters.
 How Long Does a Tundra Engine Replacement Take? 
 It depends on engine availability and how busy your dealer is. Josh's dealer gave him a rental and told him to expect the work to take a few weeks.
 Waits have varied widely. Another group member, Melissa Tacher, said her family's two Tundras were handled about a year apart. "Toyota did a recall on both of our truck engines. They sent notices and the we had to wait to get them installed as they had to build each engine. They went by year so all the 2022 across the board got done first then the 2023 models. There was about a year between my husband's truck engine replacement and mine being done," she wrote.
 If your truck is scheduled for an engine replacement, ask your dealer these questions:
 Is the replacement engine in stock, or on order?
 How long will the truck be in the shop?
 Will Toyota provide a rental or loaner while I wait?
 What warranty coverage applies to the replacement engine?
 Will I get paperwork showing the recall was completed?
 Can a Used Car Dealer Sell a Truck With an Open Recall? 
 Yes, in most cases. Federal rules prevent dealers from selling new vehicles with unrepaired safety recalls, but there is no federal rule stopping the sale of used vehicles with open recalls .
 Advertising 
 That applies to online retailers, traditional used car lots and private sellers alike. It is up to the buyer to check, which is exactly why Josh's story is worth sharing.
 Before you buy any used 2022 to 2024 Tundra, do this:
 Run the VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls before you sign
 Ask the seller in writing whether the engine recall was completed
 Ask for dealer paperwork showing the engine replacement or inspection
 Have a Toyota dealer run the VIN for Toyota specific campaigns
 If the recall is open, factor in the time without the truck
 Does a Recall Engine Replacement Hurt Resale Value? 
 A completed recall with paperwork is usually a good thing, because a buyer knows the engine was replaced or cleared. An open recall, or a history of engine trouble, can hurt value, as one owner learned when his trade in offer came in nearly $10,000 lower after an engine failure .
 Owners have also noticed that recall fixes can affect how buyers see these trucks. Torque News reported on how the Tundra V6 recall software fix has been costing owners resale value , so keep every document from your recall visit.
 Tundra Owners Still Love Their Trucks 
 Not every recall story ends with frustration. Melissa and her husband had both of their Tundras fixed and remain big fans.
 "We have a 2022 Toyota Tundra 1794 Edition and a 2023 Toyota Tundra 1794 Edition, exact same package and interior color just different years and exterior colors. Great trucks and we love them!" she wrote.
 For Josh, the timing turned a routine alignment into a new engine at no cost, with only a few weeks in a rental. That is about the best way an open recall can be discovered.
 Tundra Engine Recall Facts at a Glance 
 First recall: May 2024, NHTSA campaign 24V381
 Vehicles in first recall: 102,092, including 98,568 Tundras and 3,524 Lexus LX600s
 Model years in first recall: 2022 and 2023 non hybrid
 Cause: Machining debris left inside the engine during manufacturing
 Remedy: Free engine replacement
 Second recall: About 127,000 more 2022 to 2024 Tundra, LX and 2024 GX vehicles
 Second recall remedy: Bearing inspection, with engine replacement if needed
 Hybrid Tundras: Not included
 Used vehicles: Can legally be sold with open recalls under federal rules
 Did your Tundra get a new engine under the recall? How long did you wait, and did your dealer give you a rental? Let us know in the comments below.
